title: Genomic Characterization and Protective Efficacy of a Lytic Phage Cocktail Against Vibrio anguillarum in Rainbow Trout Aquaculture
content:
ABSTRACT

Aquaculture needs alternatives to antibiotics against vibriosis caused by Vibrio anguillarum. Three lytic bacteriophages, VP-BES, VP-ALA and VP-SUMAE, were isolated from Turkish aquaculture waters. Their genome sequences (54,898, 129,979 and 71,257 bp, respectively) lacked detectable antibiotic resistance, virulence or lysogeny genes, consistent with a lytic lifestyle; for VP-ALA and VP-SUMAE, only partial assemblies (estimated 84.2% and 76.1% complete) were screened. Intergenomic similarities of 2.4%–23.8% to their closest characterized relatives indicate three new species in two proposed new genera, one for VP-BES (≤ 0.3% to the other isolates) and one for VP-ALA and VP-SUMAE (Ackermannviridae; 70.2% mutual similarity, marginally above the 70% genus threshold). All three lysed all eight V. anguillarum strains but none of 18 non-target strains, and none was cytotoxic to EPC cells. In intraperitoneally challenged rainbow trout (Oncorhynchus mykiss), 10-day survival rose significantly from 13.3% (untreated) to 86.7% with a three-phage cocktail injected intraperitoneally immediately after challenge and 73.3% with cocktail-supplemented feed from 2 days post-infection (relative percentage survival 84.6% and 69.2%). Route, timing and delivered dose differed between treatments, and tissue bacterial loads were not measured; the data therefore show protection against mortality, not route effect or bacterial clearance. These phages are promising candidates against trout vibriosis.
